notes: (1) Section 12 sets the Act's effective date at July 1, 2050, which looks like a placeholder. Section 2 still applies to tax years after December 31, 2026, and Part II takes effect January 1, 2029. The bracket schedules are modeled from their own tax-year headings (2027 and 2029), not from the 2050 date. (2) The text has no sunset for the Section 1 brackets, so both vintages are modeled through 2031. (3) Section 12 repeals the Section 2 child and dependent care changes on December 31, 2032, which is past the modeled window. (4) Section 3 leaves the new Act 163 repeal date blank. The spec therefore sets neither credits.eitc_percent nor credits.food_excise: under current law the EITC reverts to 20% and the food/excise credit to the pre-Act 163 table after tax year 2027. (5) The definition of adjusted gross income in Section 2(h) is definition-only and is not listed as a provision. (6) Part II credits are not modeled. Several already lapse under their own terms: the high technology credit and the technology infrastructure credit end after 2010, and the ship repair credit ends after 2026. (7) The description names the research activities credit. No section here repeals it directly; Section 10 only moves up the effective date of Act 261 Part II. Whether that Part repeals the research credit is inferred from the description and is not shown in the bill text.
